name: building energy consumption benchmark
description: In this study, we investigate the application of Prophet, an open-source forecasting tool, to predict electricity energy consumption using a substantial benchmark dataset. The considered benchmark dataset includes time series data from electricity meters in hourly resolution from 200 buildings. Accurate energy usage prediction is essential for efficient energy management and sustainability. Our computational analysis showcases the capabilities and limitations of Prophet in capturing the intricate patterns in energy consumption data. Through a comprehensive evaluation employing nested cross-validation for time series, we highlight the model’s performance.
evaluation_method: forecast error metrics such as MAE, RMSE, and MAPE
typical_sota_score: MAPE ~5–15% (varies by building and forecast horizon; some setups report lower or higher errors)
reputation: A practical applied forecasting benchmark used in energy analytics, but not a widely standardized community benchmark.
notes: Small-to-moderate scale building energy dataset; results depend heavily on preprocessing, seasonality, and train/test split choices.
